task_spec:
> Using the Global Weather Repository CSV, produce:
> 1. Two ranked bar charts of the **top 10 hottest cities**, one by average and one by single hottest measurement temperature (celsius)
> 2. Two ranked bar charts of the **top 10 hottest countries**, one by average and one by single hottest measurement temperature (celsius)
> 3. **Print the top 10 lists to the console** before plotting: for each of the 4 charts, print the ranked names and their temperature values (e.g., "1. Paris: 25.2 deg C")
> 4. A **100-word summary** for a non-technical audience explaining the rankings and any notable patterns
>
> Column reference: cities are in `location_name`, countries in `country`, temperature in `temperature_celsius`.

report_draft: The Global Weather Repository reveals striking geographic patterns in extreme heat. By average temperature, the Middle Eastern cities of Ar Riyadh (45.0°C) and Kuwait (44.4°C) top the list, alongside desert and tropical cities like Doha, Abu Dhabi, and Bangkok. When measuring single hottest readings, Kuwait City (49.2°C) and Baghdad (49.1°C) lead realistically hot extremes—except for one notable anomaly: Suva, Fiji recorded 79.3°C, likely a data error (Fahrenheit misrecorded as Celsius). By country, Saudi Arabien dominates average temperatures at 45.0°C, with Marrocos and Turkménistan following. For maximum readings, Fiji Islands registers that same implausible 79.3°C spike, while Kuwait and Iraq show realistic Gulf region extremes. The clear pattern: Middle Eastern and North African nations consistently occupy top rankings, reflecting their arid climates and intense solar exposure.

report_history.content: The Global Weather Repository reveals striking geographic patterns in extreme heat. By average temperature, the Middle Eastern cities of Ar Riyadh (45.0°C) and Kuwait (44.4°C) top the list, alongside desert and tropical cities like Doha, Abu Dhabi, and Bangkok. When measuring single hottest readings, Kuwait City (49.2°C) and Baghdad (49.1°C) lead realistically hot extremes—except for one notable anomaly: Suva, Fiji recorded 79.3°C, likely a data error (Fahrenheit misrecorded as Celsius). By country, Saudi Arabien dominates average temperatures at 45.0°C, with Morocco, Turkmenistan, and Turkey following. For maximum readings, Fiji Islands registers that same implausible 79.3°C spike, while Kuwait and Iraq show realistic Gulf region extremes. The clear pattern: Middle Eastern and North African nations consistently occupy top rankings, reflecting their arid climates and intense solar exposure.
